sourceRun.label: Primary release evidence review
sourceRun.method: Agent review of canonical release timestamps, published roadmap, complete governance histories and operator deployment receipts

candidates.label: Tezos X Mainnet
candidates.summary: Etherlink kernel 7.1 has a completed mainnet deployment receipt. The official roadmap still labels activation Planned. Its Q3 target has elapsed; the broader launch remains unconfirmed in this review.
candidates.nextSignal: Explicit full Tezos X rollout declaration tied to the deployed kernel and operator compatibility
candidates.highlight: Ganesha introduced the Michelson/NAC infrastructure proposal. Confirmed kernel deployment and the broader Tezos X rollout remain separate claims.

gates.label: Runtime hardening
gates.detail: Ganesha describes the Michelson interface and native atomic composability; kernel deployment does not establish completion of the wider Tezos X roadmap.

gates.label: Previewnet stability
gates.detail: October 27 review: Previewnet outbox recovered October 26 at 11:33:12 UTC. Later The Graph incidents were separate. Stability remains validating; recovery does not confirm the full rollout.

gates.label: Node and tooling compatibility
gates.detail: EVM node 0.67 is published. Ganesha required at least 0.64 and a restart to expose Michelson RPCs after activation; each operator remains responsible for compatibility.

gates.label: Mainnet proposal readiness
gates.detail: Ganesha was publicly proposed for the SLOW track. The reviewed archive contains SLOW proposal 40 and promotion 41; the old no-public-proposal claim is retracted.

gates.label: Etherlink governance
gates.detail: FAST 636/637 record the kernel 7.1 proposal and promotion. Newer FAST 693/694 record a September 16 proposal and promotion; governance receipts alone do not establish the full Tezos X rollout.

gates.label: Production rollout
gates.detail: Etherlink reports kernel 7.1 mainnet maintenance completed August 29. Its deployment is confirmed; a separate declaration of the full Tezos X rollout is still required.

evidence.label: Current official Tezos X roadmap
evidence.note: The page still labels mainnet activation Q3 2026 and Planned. That target quarter has elapsed; the unchanged page neither confirms a full rollout nor supplies a replacement date.

evidence.label: Ganesha proposal and scope
evidence.note: The July 31 post describes Michelson/NAC infrastructure, a SLOW-track proposal, the 0.64 operator minimum and a separate later full Tezos X rollout.

evidence.label: Complete official SLOW period archive
evidence.note: SLOW 40/41 record the August proposal and promotion. Period 41 has Nay-dominant voting power; its result must not be conflated with later FAST votes.

evidence.label: Complete official FAST period archive
evidence.note: FAST 636/637 retain the August 28 kernel vote. New September 16 periods 693/694 record proposal 009e07373751a43acbf0cd747b404f45130e0ad561c4b7da937e02eb812bd0f7e8. Votes alone do not prove deployment or a full-platform launch.

evidence.label: Etherlink 7.1 mainnet deployment
evidence.note: Official maintenance names kernel 7.1 mainnet activation, beginning August 29 at 19:45:14 UTC and ending at 20:45:14 UTC. This is an operator deployment receipt.

evidence.label: Tezos X documentation scope
evidence.note: The landing page now says documentation is being prepared for the upcoming launch and links Etherlink docs. This replaces the prior experimental-testnet description without declaring the full launch complete.

evidence.label: EVM node 0.67 release receipt
evidence.note: The canonical release record identifies version 0.67 and released_at 2026-09-29T09:30:34.058Z, upcoming_release false, and static binaries. Publication is distinct from the full Tezos X rollout.

evidence.label: September 24 Shadownet kernel maintenance
evidence.note: The completed September 24 maintenance names Ganesha-r2 and Shadownet services, from 15:10 to 16:10 UTC. This testnet receipt does not establish mainnet deployment or the full Tezos X launch.

evidence.label: October 6 Michelson RPC maintenance
evidence.note: Resolved mainnet and Shadownet RPC maintenance moved a public IP address. This infrastructure operation does not announce a kernel activation or full Tezos X rollout.

evidence.label: October 8 Previewnet hardware maintenance
evidence.note: Resolved hardware maintenance restored Blockscout Previewnet redundancy at 11:02 UTC. This testnet infrastructure receipt does not confirm mainnet release scope.

evidence.label: October 14 Previewnet and Shadownet outage
evidence.note: Resolved October 15 at 08:38 UTC after services recovered from 08:29. The incident began October 14 at 06:32 UTC; Mainnet was not listed as affected. Recovery does not certify sustained stability.

evidence.label: October 26 Previewnet and The Graph recoveries
evidence.note: Previewnet outbox: 11:32:07–11:33:12 UTC. Later The Graph Studio and Studio API incidents recovered by 21:09:34 UTC. Mainnet block production was not listed as affected; no full-launch inference.

history.reason: EVM node 0.64 shipped and advanced tooling compatibility; confidence did not rise because the public mainnet proposal is still absent.
Previewnet kernel 0.8 shipped, but the reviewed FAST governance window still has no winning mainnet-kernel candidate.
Kernel 0.9 was cut on master and the Previewnet installer was corrected, but the reviewed FAST governance window still has no winning mainnet-kernel candidate.

Retracted the earlier FAST-null inference after reviewing SLOW/FAST histories and the 7.1 deployment. Q3 remains an official target; conflicting rollout documentation lowers confidence in the full-launch forecast.
September 8: releases and complete SLOW/FAST archives unchanged. Kernel 7.1 remains separate from Q3 target and experimental-testnet docs; full rollout unconfirmed.

September 23: EVM node 0.66 is published and FAST 693/694 add a September 16 vote. Documentation is being prepared for an upcoming launch; the roadmap still says Q3 Planned. Kernel 7.1 deployment remains confirmed, but the broader launch is unconfirmed.
September 25: releases and complete governance archives unchanged. Ganesha-r2 maintenance is Shadownet-only. Roadmap Q3 Planned; docs pending; full mainnet launch unconfirmed.
September 27: complete SLOW/FAST archives unchanged; latest maintenance Shadownet-only. Q3 Planned and docs pending; kernel deployment does not confirm full rollout.
September 28: Q3 activation remains Planned and launch docs pending. SLOW/FAST archives are unchanged, latest maintenance is Shadownet-only, and the full rollout is unconfirmed.
September 29: EVM 0.67 published. Q3 Planned and docs pending; complete SLOW/FAST archives unchanged; latest maintenance Shadownet-only. Full Tezos X launch unconfirmed.

October 1: Q3 elapsed; roadmap still says Planned and docs upcoming launch. Complete SLOW/FAST histories unchanged; release tags and deployment receipts do not confirm full Tezos X rollout. No replacement date inferred.

October 3: roadmap still says Q3 Planned after the target elapsed; docs say upcoming launch. Complete SLOW/FAST histories and deployment receipts unchanged; no full rollout or replacement date confirmed.
October 14: an unresolved Previewnet/Shadownet outage blocks the stability gate. Full mainnet rollout remains unconfirmed.
October 15: Previewnet/Shadownet recovered at 08:38 UTC. Stability returns to validating; the full mainnet rollout remains unconfirmed.
October 26: Previewnet outbox recovered at 11:33:12 UTC after a 65-second incident. Stability remains validating; full mainnet rollout remains unconfirmed.
October 27: operator expanded the October 26 incident with later The Graph outages, recovered by 21:09:34 UTC. Previewnet recovery remains 11:33:12 UTC; full launch unconfirmed.

methodology: Octez, the EVM node, Tezos X Previewnet, kernel governance, kernel deployment and the full Tezos X rollout remain separate claims.
Confidence comes from direct artifacts and coordinated evidence, never raw merge volume or a completion percentage.
The published Q3 2026 roadmap target has elapsed. No replacement date or full-rollout completion is inferred from an unchanged roadmap or deployed kernel infrastructure.
Governance review checks complete SLOW and FAST histories. An empty current FAST window cannot prove that no public proposal or governance vote has ever existed.
releasedAt uses the canonical release record publication clock, never a source commit timestamp. Review timestamps describe this review and do not refresh upstream facts.
The browser renders reviewed evidence, marks the receipt stale after 36 hours and removes it at expiry. Extending those clocks requires another substantive source review.
